title: UNComp: Uncertainty-aware KV-Cache Compression for Long-Context LLM Inference
one_line_claim: Proposes truncated matrix entropy to measure uncertainty in token representations, enabling adaptive two-stage KV-cache compression that achieves 4.74% cache retention while maintaining quality.
method_summary: UNComp measures uncertainty in hidden states and attention heads using truncated matrix entropy (derived from spectral decomposition). It applies a two-stage compression strategy: first, evicts low-entropy hidden states based on a learned threshold; second, compresses KV heads using per-head entropy scores with dynamic token eviction. The method is tested on Llama2/3 and Qwen2.5 models across LongBench tasks.

key_findings.finding: Achieves extreme compression with minimal quality degradation: 4.74% compression ratio while maintaining performance comparable to full KV-cache on long-context benchmarks.
Two-stage compression strategy identifies and preserves high-entropy heads (retrieval heads/layers) that are critical for maintaining model performance.
key_findings.quote: we propose a two-stage compression strategy... adaptively selecting high-entropy hidden states and KV pairs based on their information content measured by TME

key_findings.finding: Truncated matrix entropy (TME) provides a theoretically grounded uncertainty measure that outperforms simpler alternatives in extreme compression scenarios, with superiority demonstrated over CHAI and other baselines.
key_findings.quote: truncated matrix entropy (TME), a novel metric to measure uncertainty in matrices by quantifying information retained after truncation... comprehensive experiments on LongBench demonstrate the superiority of UNComp over existing methods

relation_to_herald.shared: Both leverage per-token distributional signals (entropy, logit variance) as runtime features to guide model behavior Both operate during generation without retraining, extracting information from forward pass outputs Both focus on long-context or memory-intensive scenarios where computational/memory efficiency is critical
differs_on: Goal: UNComp optimizes compression efficiency during normal inference; HERALD predicts catastrophic failures caused by compression-induced KV eviction
Signal usage: UNComp uses entropy to decide which tokens to keep (optimization); HERALD uses logit features to forecast looping/non-termination before onset
Failure detection: UNComp does not explicitly detect or predict catastrophic failures; HERALD's core thesis is early hazard prediction to enable intervention
